payload.claim: `regate(task_id)` silently returns `None` when `record_key(task_id)` is `None` (an id naming no task), diverging from every other per-task reader in this file that performs the identical `record_key` check and reads the same way (`qualifications` at line ~1801, `spec_texts` at line ~1957, and the single-spec-text reader at line ~1946), each of which raises `ValueError(f"no task {task_id} to ...")` for exactly this case. `record_regate` itself raises for an unknown task id (per its own docstring and the spec's wording), so the write and read halves of the same feature disagree on how an unknown task is reported, and the read half breaks the file's own established convention (CLAUDE.md's 'Import ... from the module that defines it' / one-source principle, applied here to behavior rather than a symbol): a caller passing a stale or mistyped task id gets a silent `None` indistinguishable from 'this task has no re-gate yet' instead of the explicit error every sibling reader would give.
